system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The detailed prompt design and instruction templates of the task planning agent are provided in Appendix A.1.
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt templates mentioned; appendix not included in evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: the designer specifies design requirements and constraints through natural language input
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/file navigation; design database is used by models, not injected as environment context.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The results are visualized in the front -end interface, enabling rapid comparison and evaluation of different design schemes.
observation_format.note: Visualizations go to the user interface; observations to the LLM appear textual.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: the functional agents are responsible for generative geometry design, rapid performance prediction, multi -objective optimization, and physics -based validation
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool described; tools are simulation/generation tools.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: a graph-structured agent framework that enables efficient integration of LLMs with external tools, APIs, and databases
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in the paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the agent autonomously constructs an iterative optimization workflow with feedback loops, demonstrating its capabilities for result-driven decision-making and adaptive planning
loop_primitives.note: Supervisor plans then delegates; CFD/prediction validation feeds back into optimization.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: It effectively maps unstructured natural language inputs into structured graph -based workflows and adaptively adjusts planning strategies according to task requirements.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The proposed framework adopts a supervisor -based architecture. A high- level planning agent is responsible for global task scheduling and decomposes complex turbomachinery aerodynamic design problems into multiple subtasks.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: It can also selectively invoke the compressor design agent, performance prediction agent, and optimization agent at appropriate stages.
delegation_mechanism.note: Fixed set of agent nodes in a graph; control routed to them rather than spawning new agents.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: After completion, the agent prompts the user for post-processing. Upon confirmation, it automatically generates a script compatible with ANSYS CFX-Post
human_in_loop.note: Also: "human feedback can be introduced as external input to guide the agents in handling ambiguous design decisions"; end-to-end run reported without intervention.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: these frameworks decompose design processes into subtasks using role allocation, state management, and tool invocation
short_term_state.note: LangGraph graph state inferred; not explicitly described for TurboAgent.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The database used in this study, derived from [33], is based on a prototype of a transonic 1.5- stage compressor rotor blade.
long_term_memory.note: Database is training data for models, not cross-run agent memory; no memory mechanism reported.

self_verification.evidence_quote: the physics validation agent performs automated CFD simulations on the generated candidates
self_verification.note: CFD/FEA simulation is the harness-run verification analogous to test execution.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Convergence is assumed when the improvement in the best performance remains below a predefined threshold for J consecutive generations.
retry_policy.note: Optimization loop retriggered if validation results do not meet targets.

rollback.evidence_quote: Update the historical best design if improvement is found.
rollback.note: No undo/revert mechanism described; best-design tracking only.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: if convergence criteria are met (e.g., improvement smaller than 𝜀𝜀 for 𝐽𝐽 consecutive generations) then break;
termination_condition.note: Also generation cap Gmax in Algorithm 2; workflow ends when planning agent declares the task completed.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: the total token consumption for completing the full workflow, from design generation t o simulation- based validation, is approximately 80,000 to 100,000 tokens
cost_controls.note: Cost is measured but no budget/caching/routing mechanism reported.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Under parallel execution with 30 CPU cores, the simulation time for a single operating condition is a pproximately 30 minutes.
timeouts.note: Runtime reported, no enforced timeouts described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: These processes are implemented through interactions between the agent and CFD/FEA software APIs.
execution_isolation.note: Local commercial solvers (AutoGrid5, CFX) invoked on the host; no isolation described.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: it automatically constructs a workflow that includes mesh generation, preprocessing, and solver execution

network_policy.evidence_quote: By leveraging different LLM APIs, the agent interprets natural language inputs provided by the user.
network_policy.note: No network policy mentioned in the paper.

permission_model.evidence_quote: the entire workflow operates wit hout explicit human intervention, achieving seamless task transitions and dynamic adjustments across multiple stages

tracing.evidence_quote: the LLM can generate structured summaries of the design process and automatically produce design reports
tracing.note: Reports and front-end visualization; no trace format described.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: A transonic single -rotor compressor is used as the validation case to systematically assess the proposed framework.
eval_hooks.note: Case-study validation only; no benchmark evaluation runner reported.

guardrails.evidence_quote: When constraints are violated, penalties are computed as linear functions of the normalized deviation.
guardrails.note: Design constraints act as optimization penalties, not safety guardrails; no filters reported.

target_domain.evidence_quote: an LLM -driven autonomous multi -agent framework for turbomachinery aerodynamic design and optimization
target_domain.note: Engineering design domain; closest to research/other.

open_source.evidence_quote: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: By leveraging different LLM APIs, the agent interprets natural language inputs provided by the user.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: this study proposes TurboAgent, a large language model (LLM)-driven autonomous multi-agent framework

first_release_date.evidence_quote: TurboAgent: An LLM-Driven Autonomous Multi-Agent Framework for Turbomachinery Aerodynamic Design
first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv id 2604.06747 implies April 2026; no release tag.
